turns.text: Not yet. We both needed some space. Bob went for a drive, and I've just been trying to calm down.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Taking some space can be helpful to gather thoughts. Do you think you’ll be ready to talk soon?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I hope so. I don't want to keep ignoring it, but I'm also scared it'll turn into another argument.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That's understandable. Talking during a calm moment might help. Maybe planning a time to chat could prevent it from escalating?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That's a good idea. Maybe after dinner tonight. I just wish he would understand how stressed I am too.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Your feelings are very valid, Emily. It's important for both of you to feel heard. Do you feel like you can express how you’re both feeling?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I want to, but sometimes I don’t know how to start without sounding like I’m blaming him.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Starting with 'I feel' statements can help focus on your emotions rather than assigning blame. It's okay to express vulnerability.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That's true. I'll try that. Thanks for reminding me. I just want us to be okay.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: You’re doing your best, and that is important. Figuring it out together might bring you closer. How are you taking care of yourself today?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I haven’t really done much for myself yet. Maybe I should go for a walk or listen to some music.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That sounds like a wonderful idea. Taking a little time for self-care can help clear your mind and give you strength.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thanks for listening. It really helps just having someone to talk to about all this.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm always here for you, Emily. Take it one step at a time, and keep me updated if you need anything.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I will. Thanks again.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Hey Emily, it's been a little while. How are you doing?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Hi, it's been... a tough week.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm sorry to hear that. Do you want to talk about what's been going on?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, actually. My son Jerry got in trouble at school. They caught him using his phone inappropriately.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That sounds really stressful. How did you find out about it?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: We had a meeting with the school's principal. It was embarrassing, especially after telling him so many times to focus on his studies.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I can imagine how difficult that must have been for you. How did the meeting go?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: It was tense. The principal was understanding but firm. I just felt so disappointed and a bit like I've failed him.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It's understandable to feel that way, but you haven't failed him. You're a caring mother who's trying her best.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thank you. I've been trying to figure out how to handle this. The financial strain with Bob, and now Jerry acting out... it's just a lot.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That does sound overwhelming. How have you been managing everything?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Therapy helps, but outside of that, I just try to keep my head above water.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm glad you've found some support in therapy. What strategies have been helping you there?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: The therapist has been teaching me breathing techniques and we've been working on expressing my feelings more constructively.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That sounds really valuable. Do you think any of those techniques could help with how you're feeling about Jerry?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Perhaps. I think I need to communicate better with him and find out what's really going on beneath the surface.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It sounds like you have a great approach. Being able to talk openly with him might really help both of you.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I hope so. I just want to make sure he understands that I care about him, even when I’m upset.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: He’s fortunate to have you watching out for him. If you ever need to talk more about any of this, I’m here for you.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thank you. It means a lot to have someone to lean on right now.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Hey, I really need to talk. Things have been so overwhelming lately.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm here for you, Emily. What's been going on?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Jerry left us. It was so sudden after a huge argument, and I feel lost.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: I'm so sorry to hear that. It must be incredibly hard for you. Do you want to talk about what led to the disagreement?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: We were arguing about his lack of responsibility and how he's ignoring his future. Maybe I was too harsh.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It sounds like you're worried about his well-being and future, which is completely understandable. How are you feeling about the situation now?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I'm torn. Part of me feels guilty, but another part feels exhausted from all the stress we've been through.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It's okay to feel mixed emotions. You're dealing with a lot on your plate—work, family, and financial pressures. It's understandable to feel overwhelmed.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Yeah, with Bob's job, Jerry's incident at school, and all... it feels never-ending. I just want a break.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: You've been through an extraordinary amount. Can your therapy sessions provide a space to process these feelings?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: They're helpful, but it's hard to shake the constant anxiety. I just wish Jerry was back home so we could work things out.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: It sounds like you really value the connection with your family. Have you tried reaching out to Jerry since he left?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: I have, but he hasn't responded. It breaks my heart knowing he's out there, upset and alone.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Feeling powerless in this situation can be stressful. Is there anyone else you can lean on for support during this time?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Bob's trying his best, but we both feel so drained. It's tough to even find time for us to talk deeply anymore.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Finding moments to connect amidst the chaos sounds challenging. Maybe even small shared moments with Bob could provide some comfort?

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: That's true. Even just sitting together, watching something light, might ease the tension.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: That sounds like a good start. Remember, you're doing your best in a tough situation. It's okay to take small steps and be kind to yourself.

turns.speaker: seeker
turns.text: Thank you, that really helps. I guess I just have to keep trying and hope things will get better.

turns.speaker: supporter
turns.text: Absolutely, Emily. Keep holding on to that hope, and I'm here for you whenever you need to talk.
